enum.name: MAV_COLLISION_ACTION
enum.description: Possible actions an aircraft can take to avoid a collision.

entry.name: MAV_COLLISION_ACTION_ASCEND_OR_DESCEND
entry.description: Ascend or Descend to avoid threat

entry.name: MAV_COLLISION_ACTION_MOVE_PERPENDICULAR
entry.description: Aircraft to move perpendicular to the collision's velocity vector

entry.name: MAV_COLLISION_ACTION_RTL
entry.description: Aircraft to fly directly back to its launch point

entry.name: MAV_COLLISION_THREAT_LEVEL_LOW
entry.description: Craft is mildly concerned about this threat

entry.name: MAV_COLLISION_THREAT_LEVEL_HIGH
entry.description: Craft is panicking, and may take actions to avoid threat

enum.name: MAV_COLLISION_SRC
enum.description: Source of information about this collision.

entry.name: MAV_COLLISION_SRC_MAVLINK_GPS_GLOBAL_INT
entry.description: ID field references MAVLink SRC ID

message.name: COLLISION
message.field: Unique identifier, domain based on src field
Action that is being taken to avoid this collision
How concerned the aircraft is about this collision
Closest vertical distance between vehicle and object
Closest horizontal distance between vehicle and object

message.name: V2_EXTENSION
message.description: Message implementing parts of the V2 payload specs in V1 frames for transitional support.
message.field: A code that identifies the software component that understands this message (analogous to USB device classes or mime type strings). If this code is less than 32768, it is considered a 'registered' protocol extension and the corresponding entry should be added to https://github.com/mavlink/mavlink/definition_files/extension_message_ids.xml. Software creators can register blocks of message IDs as needed (useful for GCS specific metadata, etc...). Message_types greater than 32767 are considered local experiments and should not be checked in to any widely distributed codebase.

Variable length payload. The length must be encoded in the payload as part of the message_type protocol, e.g. by including the length as payload data, or by terminating the payload data with a non-zero marker. This is required in order to reconstruct zero-terminated payloads that are (or otherwise would be) trimmed by MAVLink 2 empty-byte truncation. The entire content of the payload block is opaque unless you understand the encoding message_type. The particular encoding used can be extension specific and might not always be documented as part of the MAVLink specification.

message.name: MEMORY_VECT
message.description: Send raw controller memory. The use of this message is discouraged for normal packets, but a quite efficient way for testing new messages and getting experimental debug output.
message.field: Starting address of the debug variables
Version code of the type variable. 0=unknown, type ignored and assumed int16_t. 1=as below
Type code of the memory variables. for ver = 1: 0=16 x int16_t, 1=16 x uint16_t, 2=16 x Q15, 3=16 x 1Q14

message.name: DEBUG_VECT
message.description: To debug something using a named 3D vector.
message.field: Timestamp (UNIX Epoch time or time since system boot). The receiving end can infer timestamp format (since 1.1.1970 or since system boot) by checking for the magnitude of the number.

message.name: NAMED_VALUE_FLOAT
message.description: Send a key-value pair as float. The use of this message is discouraged for normal packets, but a quite efficient way for testing new messages and getting experimental debug output.

message.name: NAMED_VALUE_INT
message.description: Send a key-value pair as integer. The use of this message is discouraged for normal packets, but a quite efficient way for testing new messages and getting experimental debug output.

message.name: DEBUG
message.description: Send a debug value. The index is used to discriminate between values. These values show up in the plot of QGroundControl as DEBUG N.

message.name: DEBUG_FLOAT_ARRAY
message.description: Large debug/prototyping array. The message uses the maximum available payload for data. The array_id and name fields are used to discriminate between messages in code and in user interfaces (respectively). Do not use in production code.
message.field: Timestamp (UNIX Epoch time or time since system boot). The receiving end can infer timestamp format (since 1.1.1970 or since system boot) by checking for the magnitude of the number.
Name, for human-friendly display in a Ground Control Station
Unique ID used to discriminate between arrays
